author: ViceTechnicolour
body:
Hey all,

The senior staff team has been working very hard to have everything fall into place, and there have been some new things organized to help with server feedback: it essentially knocks out two birds with one stone! Helping us collect what the community wants, while working on transparency and further developing our systems to meet your standards. While we have had this in mind for a while, it is vital we now share our sides of the story to hopefully connect the bridges that fell apart.

For this post, I'd like to introduce two new systems on the Avicus Network:

Prioritization Sheets
Managing priorities has always had things lost in the slack chat, or covered over by discussions. With this, we're working to find a proper way to organize everything that works for everyone: in this case, it's going to be having a google spreadsheet with sections for the senior mods to fill out, including IDs, priority factor, assignment, and the task. We will be taking this seriously, and work has already started as early as now to fix them. While it may not be noticeably at first, we have to improve our internal structure, and by doing this, it's beyond a huge step ahead that hopefully you guys will appreciate. Depending on the demand, and administrator approval, we could publicize this document, or have users submit them.

Feedback Sheets


Community feedback has been the demand for 2 years now: it's admitted by (some) that it's fell behind, and isn't meeting the demands it should to our customers. Whether paid or not, a sheet has been kickstarted by GrapeSmoothie, Fluenza, and I to provide speedy answers and have a structured system specifically for discussing community feedback. It contains a slot for each staff member to provide a color (red,green,blue) and text to add onto the idea. With a description, title, and some other tidbits, we're going to work our best to ensure this doesn't instantly die. These have been thrown around as well.

We may be including new systems soon, and it all depends on how we balance our workload. I'd like to note, that all of this work isn't dependent on one person, and we're all in together as a team, as the mindset should be. I would like to take this moment and say, as well, we hope you all are starting to understand our situation. We're hard workers!
